notes_in.text: Reversing while watching the camera and steering by the gap between the rails worked well through the right-hand turn: smooth, never stopped. Near the bay it went wrong. The rails closed in, the gap logic panicked and swung the trailer sharply right, and the trailer's rear-left corner touched the end wall. Next time, once the painted bay corners show on the camera, stop chasing gaps. Aim between the corners, straighten the trailer early, creep slowly and stop before the end wall. The trailer is short and reacts fast, so make gentle corrections.

Disaster: sign errors early on swung the trailer the wrong way. After that, endless pull-forwards and rewrites used up every touch, and the car's rear-left corner kept hitting the outer left rail in the right bend. Get the steering sign right from the start and check it with a short check-in. Begin the right swing early but gently, and keep the whole car in the middle of the corridor, watching the car's corners as well as the trailer's. Prefer one smooth, slow controller over many replacements, and avoid gear changes. Tip: this trailer is short and twitchy, so use small hitch angles and creep.

Same failure again. My gap-following controller had its sign backwards at the start and swung the trailer left into the rail. In the right bend, letting the hitch get large swung the car's nose into the outer left rail over and over. Then many pull-forwards and rewrites burned all the time. Priorities: check the sign with a short creep straight back first. Reverse straight down the middle, start the right swing gently and keep the hitch moderate. Keep the car on the inner side and watch its front-left corner. Tip: this short trailer folds fast, so creep and correct early.

Last time failed: the course bends toward the trailer's left soon after the start. The trailer went straight past the bend and its rear-right corner hit the outer rail again and again. Then the tractor's front-right swung into the rail while chasing the trailer. Start the left swing early and gently and keep the hitch angle moderate. Measure a pull-forward by distance moved, not time, since the gear change eats the time. Get the steering right early instead of constant rewrites. Tip: this short trailer reacts fast, so reverse slowly and correct small angles early.

Aiming for the widest gap got through the S-bend cleanly, but near the bay the trailer's rear-left kept hitting the left rail, and a straight forward pull scraped the tractor's front-left. Constant controller rewrites there wasted time. What finally worked: pull forward briefly until straight, then reverse slowly along a fixed straight line well to the right, watching the right mirror, where the painted bay corners show. Priority: before the last stretch, get over to the right and line up straight early instead of chasing gaps. Tip: keep the hitch angle small and go slowly near the bay.

Never got past the first left bend; disqualified on touches. Holding a big hitch angle there swings the trailer's front-right corner into the right rail, and the tractor's nose clips the rails. Gap-chasing, mirror rail-fitting and auto shunt loops all failed and wasted time. Priority: stop early before the bend, look over both shoulders to map it, then plan one smooth arc where tractor and trailer turn together with a moderate hitch angle, starting the swing a bit later and deeper. Tip: this short trailer reacts fast, so reverse very slowly and leave margin on the right.

My early simple reverse got furthest, past halfway, before the cart's rear-left touched near the corner. Then I kept rewriting controllers, drove forward, lost ground and got stuck at the corner: reverse a little, cart folds, pull forward, repeat until time ran out. Priority: look where the course bends and map the corner early. Start the turn early and gently, keep corner speed low, never pull forward far, and keep the nose clear of the rails when pulling forward. Tip: this cart is very short and folds fast, so follow it with small quick corrections.

What worked: look back and to the right early, mark where the painted bay corners and the bay centre are, then reverse slowly so the cart axle follows the bay's centre line, looking a short way ahead and keeping a cap on the hitch angle. Do not drive forward far: the nose touched the left rail when turning forward. Tip: the cart is short, so make the corrections small and fast.

Start the bend early and gently while keeping the fold modest. Glance at the nose often, and when stuck pull forward only a little. Tip: the cart is tiny, so correct small and fast.
